structures.appearanceReference: Inspected Commercial Real Estate exterior photo: reflective blue-grey glass curtain wall, closely spaced vertical fins/mullions, distinctive sharp raised fins that step down toward the outer wings, and a dark glazed street podium partly screened by trees. Use the survey sections for exact height and setback levels; do not copy the photographed perspective as geometry.
structures.shapeRecommendation: Separate low podium from the taller, clean rectangular office volume; preserve the surveyed level breaks as setbacks only where multiple distinct section footprints support them. The survey has five components: four flat roof sections plus one small gable section at the highest edge.

The 15-33 William Street and 452-470 Flinders Street 2014 geometry bounds intersect their respective complete 2023 structure envelopes. 2014 model height/z fields and the 2023 AHD levels are separate vertical evidence and are not compared as if they shared a datum. The adjacent 474 Flinders address is not the matching 2014 polygon.

blenderWorkflow.recommendation: A separate small Blender generator should read the two groups directly from bundled public/data/buildings-raw.json, convert geographic rings with the existing origin and local-axis convention, retain all object IDs/elevation intervals as object custom properties, and create one named collection per structure. Create level bands from the official section rings, not an inferred box; keep the official polygons as a hidden reference collection. Export named GLB shells via glTF with unit scale, then manually author facade materials from verified actual photos. Do not embed downloaded third-party photos; use them as temporary modelling reference and document source URL/license/verification status. Do not edit src/data/photomesh-foreground.json.
